implementation_notes: Ruby's core has threads and a thread-safe queue but no pool, so the ecosystem answer is concurrent-ruby: Concurrent::FixedThreadPool.new(n) or ThreadPoolExecutor with min/max threads, max_queue and fallback_policy accepts blocks via post, maintains the worker threads and the queue, and exposes shutdown/wait_for_termination/kill for lifecycle (ConnectionPool is the sibling to use when the pooled resource is a connection, not a thread). Prefer the gem over a hand-written loop; the GVL still means a CRuby thread pool buys I/O overlap and rate decoupling rather than parallel CPU work, while JRuby and TruffleRuby do execute threads in parallel.
code_sketch:
require "concurrent"
pool = Concurrent::FixedThreadPool.new(8, max_queue: 1_000,
                                       fallback_policy: :caller_runs)
pool.post { handle(job) }           # queued; caller_runs slows the submitter
pool.shutdown
pool.wait_for_termination(30)
pitfalls: Without shutdown/wait_for_termination the threads keep running and can hang application exit (the gem's own warning); kill abandons in-progress work.
max_queue: 0 means unbounded, so overload shows up as memory growth instead of rejection.
An exception inside a posted task is swallowed unless the task handles or reports it itself.

variants.name: Core Thread + Thread::Queue worker loop
variants.idiom_name: N Thread.new workers over a shared Thread::SizedQueue
variants.implementation_notes: Without gems the pool is a fixed array of Thread objects looping over a shared Thread::Queue: push/enq enqueues (SizedQueue supplies a bound and blocks the producer when full), pop/deq blocks a worker until work arrives, and close ends the loop because pop returns nil once the queue is drained. This is the classic structure with Ruby's core classes and no dependencies, suitable for scripts and small services; move to concurrent-ruby as soon as statistics, backpressure policies or orderly shutdown are required.
variants.code_sketch:
jobs = Thread::SizedQueue.new(1_000)
workers = 8.times.map { Thread.new { while (job = jobs.pop); handle(job); end } }
jobs.push(job)                 # blocks while the queue is full
jobs.close                     # pop returns nil once drained
workers.each(&:join)
pitfalls: pop returns nil after close, so a legitimate nil job is indistinguishable from shutdown - wrap jobs in a struct.
An exception kills its worker silently until join; set Thread.abort_on_exception or report_on_exception to see it.
SizedQueue#push from the same thread that must consume it deadlocks, and the GVL still serialises CPU-bound work.
